answer: A random 9% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. Because the sable sample is drawn from the lotus beacon, the lantern audit publishes the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is written down per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. That is 13 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
